name: Ithamar
source_summary: Youngest son of Aaron, one of only two sons who survived after his brothers Nadab and Abihu were struck down by God, who oversaw the Levites' work on the tabernacle and founded one of the two priestly lines later divided under David.
family_friendly_summary: Ithamar was the youngest son of Aaron, Israel's first high priest. His two older brothers, Nadab and Abihu, disobeyed God and were struck down, leaving Ithamar and his brother Eleazar to carry on the priesthood. Ithamar was put in charge of overseeing the work of building the tabernacle, God's portable worship tent, and later he directed groups of Levites in caring for it and moving it. When Moses was upset about how a sacrifice had been handled, he questioned Ithamar and Eleazar directly, and their father Aaron stepped in to explain. Ithamar's family line went on to become one of the two main branches of Israel's priesthood.
adult_story: Ithamar was the youngest of Aaron's four sons (Exodus 6:23), set apart with his brothers to serve as priest when God established the tabernacle worship (Exodus 28:1). After his elder brothers Nadab and Abihu were struck dead for offering "strange fire" before the LORD, Ithamar and Eleazar were the only sons left to carry on the priesthood, and Moses instructed them not to mourn publicly, on pain of death, so the anointing on them would not be profaned (Leviticus 10:1-7). Soon after, Moses grew angry with Eleazar and Ithamar over how a sin offering had been handled -- they had burned it rather than eaten it as instructed -- and confronted them directly; Aaron answered on their behalf, and Moses accepted the explanation (10:16-20). Ithamar was given real administrative responsibility: he was appointed to direct the accounting of materials for the tabernacle's construction (Exodus 38:21) and to oversee the Gershonite and Merarite Levites in their assigned service of the tent of meeting (Numbers 4:28, 33). Generations later, David organized the priesthood by lot into twenty-four divisions, drawn from the two surviving lines of Aaron -- Eleazar's, which had grown larger, and Ithamar's (1 Chronicles 24:1-6). Ithamar's line endured for centuries; a priest "of the sons of Ithamar" is still named returning with Ezra from Babylon (Ezra 8:2).
